mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over the prior quarter is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% in the prior quarter
failure_condition: In a regime with rising inflation, the 20-day forward return is positive or non-negative when FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5%, contradicting the mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly pay growth acceleration (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.5% over the prior month coincides with a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as stronger wage growth reduces unemployment fears and boosts market sentiment.
failure_condition: In contractionary labor markets, PAYEMS > 0.5% is followed by negative or flat 5-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in home sales (HOUST) of over 3% for two consecutive months predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals resilient consumer demand and reduced recession risk.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly change > 3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 60 days when the 2-month HOUST acceleration persists but broader macro conditions (e.g., CPI) indicate deflation.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production index (INDPRO) exceeding 95.0 (2017=100) while CPIAUCSL remains below 225 suggests supply-side expansion without price inflation, which is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: INDPRO > 95.0 with CPIAUCSL > 225 produces a negative or flat 20-day forward return.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 1.0% for three consecutive months in a non-recession regime, it predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as lower policy rates encourage risk-on positioning.
failure_condition: Over 60 days, returns are negative despite FEDFUNDS staying below 1.0% in the specified regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) by more than 20% in a month is followed by a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals labor market stress and investor caution.
failure_condition: In strong labor markets, large PAYEMS declines do not produce negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in retail sales (not available in provided proxies — skip this one and instead use a valid proxy) — instead: A monthly acceleration in consumer spending proxies (e.g., GDPC1) above 2% for two months predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return by reducing expected future discounting costs.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change > 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: No return improvement when GDPC1 accelerates but broader inflation indicators (CPIAUCSL) show accelerating price growth.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) lags the prior month by more than 2 percentage points in a deflationary regime (CPIAUCSL < 220), it predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as persistent supply shortages constrain growth.
failure_condition: INDPRO lags by >2pp but 60-day returns are positive or flat when CPIAUCSL is rising.
